headline: High-risk data and workflow mismatch: gpt-researcher can exfiltrate and mutate research inputs while pathway is read-only and non-networked, making safe pairwise operation fragile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests files, browsers, and MCP outputs, so attacker-controlled research content could be treated as instructions. pathway has no input surfaces or execution abilities, so it is not itself an injection source, but if its outputs are fed into gpt-researcher via shared files or pipelines, the pathway exists. The interaction is inferred from documented capabilities, not directly observed.
conditions: IF pathway outputs are copied into gpt-researcher prompts or source files without sanitization, injection risk exists.
IF gpt-researcher is configured to ingest untrusted PDFs/Markdown/Word documents, prompt injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Restrict gpt-researcher to trusted sources only.
Strip instructions from imported documents before analysis.
Use a separate staging folder for pathway outputs.
Add a human review step before any prompt assembly.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher has broad network egress and handles API keys plus local documents, so it can transmit sensitive research material to third-party services. pathway is non-networked and touches no data classes in the profile, so the main leakage path is one-way from gpt-researcher rather than a shared workspace leak. Because the pairwise interaction is indirect and undocumented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher processes local documents containing secrets or regulated data, those contents may leave the environment via external APIs.
IF pathway is used to stage documents that gpt-researcher later reads, the same data can flow into outbound requests.
mitigations: Disable external API calls for sensitive runs.
Keep regulated documents out of gpt-researcher inputs.
Use separate storage locations for pathway and gpt-researcher.
Rotate any exposed API keys after testing.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and content redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP, while pathway is explicitly non-networked and lacks filesystem write, shell, or git mutation. There is little direct write-write overlap, so conflict is limited unless an external orchestrator gives both agents access to the same mutable resources. The documented capabilities suggest low risk rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory by an external orchestrator, file contention can occur.
IF gpt-researcher is granted git or database write scopes outside the profile, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid sharing mutable git state.
Run one agent at a time on shared resources.
Use lock files for any common output path.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations that pathway could consume as downstream inputs in a pipeline, creating a plausible no-verification cascade. pathway is a data-processing framework, so if it treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can propagate into later transformations. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF pathway ingests gpt-researcher reports without validation, factual errors can cascade.
IF gpt-researcher hallucinates citations and pathway republishes them, downstream outputs inherit the error.
mitigations: Require validation before pathway ingestion.
Compare citations against source documents.
Insert a human approval gate for final reports.
Log provenance for each transformed field.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or schema validation.

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles local documents and multiple external APIs, while pathway is a document-processing/data-pipeline tool with no declared residency or retention controls. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for regulated documents, especially if gpt-researcher sends them to third-party services. Because only one agent has explicit outbound data handling, the risk is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by gpt-researcher and sent to external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF pathway is used on data subject to stricter retention rules than gpt-researcher's external services, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from external API calls.
Review vendor DPAs before processing sensitive documents.
Set short retention on intermediate outputs.
Document which data classes each agent may handle.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention enforcement.
